st: Put the lamb and beef in a large pot with [[12 cups]] cold water, the whole onion, bay leaves and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook until the meat is very tender and nearly falling off the bone.
Meanwhile, make the dough: mix the flour, eggs, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Remove the meat from the broth, cover to keep warm, and strain the broth. Remove the bones and slice the meat into pieces.
Simmer the sliced onions in [[1.5 cups]] of the broth with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper for 15 minutes until soft and silky.
Roll the dough very thin and cut it into 3-inch squares or diamonds.
Bring the remaining broth to a boil. Cook the noodle pieces in batches until tender, about 4 minutes. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Spread the noodles on a large platter, pile the meat and onion sauce on top and sprinkle with parsley. Serve with bowls of hot broth on the side.

ing: rinsed until the water runs clear, soaked 30 minutes
st: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over high heat until it is shimmering.
Add the lamb and brown it well on all sides for about 8 minutes.
Add the onions and cook until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the carrots and cook 8 minutes. Stir in the cumin, salt and pepper.
Pour in [[2 cups]] of the boiling water and simmer covered on low until the meat is tender.
Drain the soaked rice and spread it evenly over the meat and carrots without stirring. Press the whole garlic head into the center.
Gently pour [[2 cups]] boiling water down the side of the pot so it just covers the rice. Cook uncovered on high until most of the water is absorbed.
Poke a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, then mix the rice with the carrots and meat, and serve with the garlic on top.

ing: hand-pulled, or linguine or fresh udon
st: Heat the oil in a large pot over high heat. Brown the beef strips for 4 minutes and remove them.
In the same pot cook the onion and celery until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chili flakes and stir for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until thick.
Return the beef, add the potato, bell peppers, salt and [[3 cups]] water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, covered, until the beef and potato are tender.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in a big pot of boiling salted water until just tender, following the package. Drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle the beef and vegetable sauce on top. Sprinkle with cilantro.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and warm water into a stiff dough. Knead for 8 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb, onions, pumpkin, [[2 tbsp]] melted butter, [[1 tsp]] salt, cumin and pepper in a bowl until sticky.
Roll the dough very thin on a floured surface and cut into 4-inch squares.
Put a heaping spoonful of filling in the middle of each square. Bring two opposite corners together over the filling and pinch, then pinch the other two to make a pouch.
Brush a steamer basket with the oil. Set the manty in it without touching.
Steam over boiling water, covered, until the dough is translucent and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Brush with the remaining butter and serve hot with sour cream or a tomato sauce.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the lamb and brown on all sides for 8 minutes.
Season with the salt and pepper.
Lower the heat, add [[0.5 cup]] water, cover and cook slowly until the lamb is tender.
Meanwhile, fry the potatoes separately in a skillet with a little oil until golden and cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Add the onions to the lamb, stir, cover and cook until soft and sweet, about 15 minutes.
Fold in the fried potatoes and cook 3 more minutes, uncovered.
Sprinkle with fresh herbs and serve hot with flatbread.
Whisk the cornstarch with [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth. Bring [[2 cups]] water to a boil and slowly pour in the starch mixture, stirring constantly until thick and clear.
Pour into a shallow dish and cool, then refrigerate until firm like jelly.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until soft, about 5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water and chill.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Cook a thin omelet in a nonstick pan, then cool and cut into thin strips.
Cut the firm jelly into thin strips.
Mix the garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, chili oil, salt and [[3 cups]] ice water for the cold broth.
Divide the noodles, jelly, omelet and bell pepper among bowls and pour the cold broth over. Serve very cold.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and water into a smooth dough and knead 5 minutes. Rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb, onions, cumin, pepper, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] butter into a juicy filling. Chill.
Roll the dough into a big thin rectangle. Spread with the remaining softened butter, then roll up like a log and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Slice the log into 12 rounds. Press each flat and roll out into a circle about 4 inches wide.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center and fold into a triangle, pinching the edges to seal tightly.
Place on the baking sheet, brush with egg yolk and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake until golden brown and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C). Serve warm.

ing: for deep frying, plus 2 tbsp for the dough
st: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk. Let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the yeast milk and [[2 tbsp]] oil and mix into a soft dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled.
Roll the dough out to about 0.5 inch thick. Cut into diamonds or squares.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pieces in small batches, turning, until puffed and golden brown, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tea, jam or honey.

ing: or beef chuck if horse is unavailable
or beef fat or lamb fat
st: Rinse the casing under running water, then soak in warm water for 30 minutes.
Cut the meat and fat into small cubes, chill them well and chop very fine with a knife, or pulse them in a food processor.
Mix the meat and fat with the garlic, cumin, salt and pepper until evenly combined.
Slide the casing onto a sausage stuffer or funnel and fill it firmly without gaps. Tie it off into 6-inch links.
Prick the links in a few places with a pin to release air.
Bring the water to a bare simmer, around 180°F (82°C), not boiling. Lower in the sausages.
Poach until the center reaches 160°F (71°C), about 40 minutes.
Cool completely, then slice thinly. Serve cold or warm in slices with flatbread and onions.
